summary: Model legal outer-layer turns with exact discrete state and animate their presentation without using mesh transforms as the puzzle state.
objective: Let a viewer apply, inspect, undo, and replay valid face-turn sequences on a conventional 3 by 3 cube.
example_prompts: Animate R U R' U' one move at a time and let me undo each move.
Build a 3x3 cube where face buttons still mean the same thing after orbiting the camera.

claims.statement: The face letters F, B, R, L, U, D denote outer-slice quarter-turns; prime denotes the opposite quarter-turn and suffix 2 denotes a half-turn.
claims.scope: The face-move subset of WCA notation, not wide moves or whole-puzzle rotations.

claims.statement: Clockwise is read from outside the named face; a prime move is its inverse.
claims.scope: Conventional 3 by 3 outer-face moves; the viewpoint is independent of the scene camera.

entities.name: Cubies and stickers
entities.guidance: Assign persistent identities; attach each sticker to its owning cubie and outward local normal.

entities.name: Face controls
entities.guidance: Display U, D, L, R, F, B independently of colors, with prime and half-turn choices.

entities.name: Move history
entities.guidance: Record only committed moves; expose the current turn and queue separately.

state_contract.model: Start solved. Represent each visible cubie with an exact integer grid position and an orientation from the cube rotation group; render stickers from this state.
state_contract.frame: Right-handed coordinates: R is +x, U is +y, F is +z. Opposite faces use negative axes. A clockwise turn is -90 degrees about the outward face normal.
actions: Accept only F B R L U D, each optionally followed by ASCII prime or 2; reject unsupported tokens explicitly.
Select the named outer layer from committed coordinates, rotate its positions and orientations exactly, then commit once.
Queue moves in input order; undo a committed move using its inverse. Reset cancels the current animation and queue before restoring solved state.
state_contract.authority: Discrete state owns the puzzle. An in-flight turn interpolates a presentation transform; it must not round live mesh positions into state.
state_contract.initialization: Only solved state and replay of legal supported moves are accepted. Arbitrary face-color imports require a separate reachability validator.

invariants: Each cubie identity appears once; each grid slot has one cubie and stickers retain their ownership.
Four quarter-turns of any face restore the complete state; each move followed by its inverse restores the complete state.
Unaffected cubies do not change; stickers and orientations of the moving layer rotate together.
A mixed sequence followed by the reversed sequence of inverse moves restores state. These are required implementation checks, not recorded passes.
Orbiting the camera changes no puzzle state or face identity.
motion_guidance: Animate one layer around the cube center, commit its exact endpoint once, then start the next queued move.
Pause freezes interpolation; resume finishes the same move. Reduced motion may commit immediately while showing the move label.
Rebuild the settled render from committed state after each turn to avoid accumulated transform drift.
creative_affordances: Vary background, bevels, lighting, and sticker patterns; retain distinct face labels and recognizable sticker ownership.
known_limits: No solver, arbitrary-state validation, wide moves, slice moves, or competition-grade scrambling is supplied.
Supercube center-orientation goals and physical mechanism simulation are outside this recipe.
Move conventions are source-checked; the implementation invariants remain unrun until a real player exists.
